clue.text: Who to blame when a pact goes awry

indicators.note: something gone awry is out of its proper order, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Finding someone to blame when an agreement collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awry' rearranges A PACT GOES; 'when' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A person made to carry the fault for others is the one everybody points at.

clue.text: One applauding bell ringer

explanation.surface: A spectator clapping who also rings church bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who claps hands is one, and the tongue that swings inside a bell to strike it has the same name.

clue.text: Kept going as reported in city

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the phrase is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: kept going means pressed on

explanation.surface: Persevering, so the news says, in some town.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston is a city in Lancashire, in north-west England.

clue.text: One making the bed out-of-doors

parts.note: reads like someone tidying bedding while camping outside, but the bed is a flower bed in a garden

explanation.surface: A camper making up a bed in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tending plants prepares flower beds outside.

clue.text: Like a rough cloth, flowery?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a coarse fabric might be ornate.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords a 'flower' can be something that flows, a river; the Tweed is a river on the border of England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Resembling the coarse woollen fabric tweed, and jokingly 'river-like' after the River Tweed.

clue.text: Romany salesman?

explanation.surface: A gypsy who sells goods door to door.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romany gypsy is a nomad, and a commercial representative journeying to clients was called a commercial traveller.

clue.text: Scotsman among disruptive lads taking nuts

indicators.note: one piece standing among the letters of another goes inside it
disruptive lads are disorderly, so their letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: mon is a Scots form of 'man', a crossword stand-by for a Scotsman

explanation.surface: A Scot among some unruly boys helps himself to nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disruptive' rearranges LADS to ALDS; 'among' puts MON inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Almonds are a common kind of edible kernel.

clue.text: Writes his recipe for food

indicators.note: a recipe tells how to mix ingredients, so the letters of these two words are mixed into the dish

explanation.surface: A man writes down his own cookery recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recipe for' signals that WRITES HIS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish stew is a hearty dish of mutton, potatoes and onions.

clue.text: Fly offers resistance to bird

parts.note: the warble fly is an insect whose larvae live under cattle hides
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An insect puts up a fight against a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A warbler is a small songbird.

clue.text: Cake manufactured by one with rheumatoid arthritis

parts.note: manufactured means made
I is the Roman numeral one
RA is the medical abbreviation for rheumatoid arthritis

explanation.surface: A cake baked by someone suffering from arthritis.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a firm, plain sponge traditionally eaten with a glass of the wine.

clue.text: Covetous cardinals, five have evidence of debts

parts.note: the cardinal points of the compass include E (east) and N (north)
V is the Roman numeral five
IOUs are written notes acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: Greedy churchmen, five in number, hold proof of what they owe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinals' suggests churchmen, but it means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A covetous person wants what others have, which is jealousy of their possessions.

clue.text: Spotted by a mudslinger?

parts.note: spotted seems to mean noticed, but read literally someone hurling mud leaves you covered in specks

explanation.surface: Being noticed by a political smear merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: Splashed with drops, as by flung mud, is to be covered in spots.

clue.text: Chained excited animal

indicators.note: an excited creature thrashes about, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

explanation.surface: A chained beast grows agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna is a spiny egg-laying mammal of Australia and New Guinea.

clue.text: Rides round present day islands

indicators.note: one piece goes round another, enclosing it

parts.note: rides on a bike, cycles
AD (anno Domini) marks the present era

explanation.surface: Bike tours around modern-day islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclades are a group of Greek islands in the Aegean.

clue.text: Penny hurried to church with swagger

parts.note: hurried means ran
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A woman called Penny dashes off to church with a strut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a name but is the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To prance is to walk with a showy, self-important strut.

clue.text: Very valuable, some say it's hilarious

explanation.surface: Something both precious and side-splitting, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some say it's' marks the second sense as colloquial, not a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond any price, and in informal speech so funny it is worth a fortune.

clue.text: Old country canal unfinished

indicators.note: an unfinished word is missing its last letter

parts.note: the Caledonian Canal runs across the Scottish Highlands

explanation.surface: An ancient realm's waterway left uncompleted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the final N of CALEDONIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia was the Roman name for Scotland, now poetic.

clue.text: Entertainer's attire's been adjusted

indicators.note: clothing that has been adjusted is altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's here is 'has', so the letters of attire plus S are the fodder

explanation.surface: A performer's costume has been altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertainer's' reads as 'Entertainer is'; 'been adjusted' rearranges ATTIRES.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional performer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Had no rent so didn't cry

explanation.surface: Someone who owed no rent and so stayed dry-eyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money for housing, but here it is a rip, a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a word with no rip, and also without weeping.

clue.text: There is as much behind as in front when this is reached

definitions.text: There is as much behind as in front when this is reached

parts.words: There is as much behind as in front when this is reached
parts.note: describes the point of a journey where the distance covered equals the distance left

explanation.surface: A riddle about a point where equal amounts lie before and after.
explanation.definitionFit: At the midpoint, the distance travelled matches the distance remaining.

clue.text: Points out nevadan city before this time

indicators.note: one piece lying out, outside, another encloses it

parts.note: E and W are compass points, east and west
Reno is a city in Nevada

explanation.surface: Indicating a city in Nevada that existed earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word meaning previously, or until now.

clue.text: Tempted during lent I ceded control

indicators.note: the answer runs during the stretch of these words, inside them

explanation.surface: Someone lured in Lent who gave up control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lent' looks like the season; 'control' completes the surface and plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Enticed means lured or drawn on with a promise.

clue.text: Waterproof garment, lubricate outer covering

parts.note: to lubricate is to oil
a skin is an outer covering

explanation.surface: A rain-proof coat and a note to grease its exterior.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilskin is a coat made of cloth treated with oil to keep out rain.

clue.text: Escort fellow with decapitated bird

parts.note: a chap is a fellow

indicators.note: a decapitated word loses its head, the first letter

parts.note: a heron is a wading bird

explanation.surface: A chaperone accompanied by a headless bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon is a companion who supervises a young person in society.

clue.text: Break the law, finish on opposite side first

indicators.note: the piece named last in the clue goes first in the answer

parts.note: in cricket the off side is opposite the leg side
finish means end

explanation.surface: A criminal who ends up on the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the off side is the half of the field opposite the leg side, facing the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend is to commit a crime or wrong.

clue.text: Unlikely explanation children might be told

explanation.surface: An implausible excuse, as you might give to youngsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a far-fetched made-up story and a magical tale read to young ones at bedtime.

clue.text: Money provided by well-dressed person at zero hour

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound in British money
provided means if
a toff is a smart upper-class person

explanation.surface: Cash donated by a dandy at the appointed moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The moment a rocket leaves the pad is the scheduled start time of a launch.

clue.text: Meal and part of it perhaps — light scone

parts.note: tea is an afternoon or evening meal
cake is one item that might be served at tea

explanation.surface: Teatime, and a part of it: a soft bun.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a light, sweet yeast bun with dried fruit, eaten toasted.

clue.text: Powerful place at the end of the line?

explanation.surface: A place of influence found at the terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: A power station is a powerful place; a train terminus is a station at the end of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A power station generates electricity, and a railway stop sits at the end of a line.

clue.text: Disagreeing with one at variance with the government

definitions.text: one at variance with the government

explanation.surface: A rebel who objects to official policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an adjective for those who differ in opinion and a noun for a political opponent of the state.
